bullets.title: NVDA: $250B OpenAI backstop, SK Group $500B+ deal, SSI investment — AI capex narrative intact
bullets.body: NVDA is reportedly in talks to provide ~$250B financing backstop for OpenAI's 10 GW Ohio data center project (total project could reach $600B), while also expanding an SK Group collaboration worth $500B+ including a 2 GW Vera Rubin data center by 2027. NVDA also invested in Safe Superintelligence and launched the Open Secure AI Alliance with Palantir, IBM, CrowdStrike, and SpaceX. Morgan Stanley frames the recent AI infrastructure selloff as 'primarily technical, not fundamental' and calls it an 'unusually attractive buying opportunity.'

bullets.title: GOOGL: UBS bullish on $700B+ NVDA/AVGO supply chain; capex backlog surges to $514B; Phillip upgrades
bullets.body: UBS flags GOOGL's capex raise and guaranteed commitments (backlog jumped from $106B to $514B in a year) as strongly bullish for semis, with NVDA and AVGO supply chain deals worth $700B+. Phillip Securities upgraded GOOGL to Accumulate (PT lowered to $425 from $450) citing strong ad growth and rapid cloud AI expansion. YouTube and Peacock Premium also struck a 2027 bundle deal under an expanded CMCSA partnership.

bullets.title: MSFT & META: Key earnings Wednesday; ~$10T in market cap reports this week
bullets.body: Microsoft reports Wednesday pre-market with consensus ~$4.21 EPS and ~$87.4B revenue (±6% implied move); Meta reports Wednesday pre-market at ~$7.20 EPS and ~$60.2B revenue. The Fed rate decision also falls Wednesday, hours before both prints. Mag 7 names were all higher in pre-market Monday (META +1.6%, MSFT +1.4%) as crude fell 7%.

bullets.title: AVGO: $200B+ Samsung contract through 2030; supply chain deals drive UBS bullish case
bullets.body: Broadcom and Samsung reportedly signed a $200B+ contract through 2030 covering <2nm foundry, next-gen HBM, advanced packaging, and custom AI/HPC silicon. UBS highlights NVDA and AVGO supply chain deals collectively worth $700B+ as the primary semiconductor demand signal. AVGO was noted as weaker technically vs. NVDA in the near term.

bullets.title: STX & WDC: MS bull case — HDD shortage pricing power, 7x CY28 EPS, buy the dip
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley sees STX and WDC trading at 7x their bull-case CY28 EPS, with a 300-400EB annual HDD supply shortfall through CY28 and CY27-28 pricing discussions moving toward $25-30/TB. STX expected to guide CY27Q1 revenue $3.80-3.85B at 53-54% gross margins; WDC at $4.05-4.15B with 54-55% GMs. HDD vendors not subject to memory-like price compression; MS frames this as a high-conviction dip-buying opportunity.

bullets.title: INTC: Seventh straight beat; AMD AI Day reinforces server leadership vs. NVDA
bullets.body: Intel delivered its seventh consecutive beat-and-raise driven by AI server demand, pricing momentum, and foundry progress. AMD's AI Day expanded its AI TAM estimate to $1.4T and showcased ROCm.AI as a direct challenge to NVIDIA's software moat, with AMD described as the server market leader. CXMT's $487B IPO debut surpassed Intel in market cap, becoming the world's 4th largest DRAM maker.

bullets.title: CHTR: Q2 misses on broadband subs and ARPU; analysts cut targets, avg PT down to $223
bullets.body: Charter Q2 EBITDA missed by 2.3% with broadband net sub losses larger than expected and below-consensus ARPU; mobile adds were the sole bright spot. UBS slashed PT to $140 from $235 (Neutral); TD Cowen cut to $380 from $413 (Buy); RBC cut to $150 from $160 (Sector Perform). Current sell-side mix is 31% Buy/46% Hold/23% Sell; EV/EBITDA of 4.9x vs. 5-year average of 7.0x.

bullets.title: VZ: Q2 postpaid beats drive guidance raise; analysts lift PTs, Citi Buy maintained
bullets.body: Verizon raised FY26 EPS guidance to $4.99-5.04 and lifted mobility/broadband service revenue growth guidance to 2.5-3.0%. Postpaid phone net adds beat by 65.8% (184K vs. 111K), and fiber net adds beat 22.1%. RBC raised PT to $47, Wells Fargo to $47, TD Cowen to $56. Citi maintains Buy, noting improving wireless competitive dynamics though LEO satellite risk (Starlink) persists.

bullets.title: APP: Citi Buy — eCommerce client count reaches 10,710 with US growth accelerating
bullets.body: AppLovin's eCommerce client count rose 1.0% WoW to 10,710 as of July 24, with US store count up 1.1% WoW to 5,051. Growth is decelerating sequentially (3.1% in 1Q26 → 1.0% 3Q26 QTD) but international markets (Germany, Hong Kong) are accelerating. Citi maintains Buy.

bullets.title: CRM: Salesforce wins $1.6B VA agentic AI deal; OpenAI Presence threatens SaaS incumbents
bullets.body: Salesforce was awarded a $1.6B three-year Agentic Enterprise License Agreement by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs, the largest agentic AI government deal to date. OpenAI's new enterprise product 'Presence' is moving beyond API access into app-layer agent deployment, raising disruption concerns for SaaS incumbents including ADBE and HUBS. Anthropic ARR estimated at ~$70B, fastest growth trajectory in tech history.

bullets.title: SHOP: Down 7.4% last week, -27.4% YTD; Canadian market weaker
bullets.body: Shopify was the notable loser in the S&P TSX Composite last week, falling 7.4% to bring YTD losses to -27.4%. In Monday pre-market, SHOP was recovering +8.3% in Canadian markets alongside broader tech relief.

bullets.title: MDB & SNOW: Premarket gains; Domo sold to Progress at 1.3x revenue; MSFT-Databricks extended
bullets.body: MDB was +2.4% and SNOW +2.6% in pre-market. Key data sector news: Domo sold its operating business to Progress Software for $400M (1.3x FY28 revenue); MSFT extended its Databricks partnership through the 2030s; Databricks raised at $188B valuation. Data/analytics stocks are down 12.5% YTD vs. S&P +8.3%.

bullets.title: TENB: Q2 earnings preview — 20-for-20 beat history, ~16.5% implied move, 50% YTD gain
bullets.body: StreetAccount consensus for TENB Q2: $264.9M revenue (vs. $263-266M guidance), $0.47 EPS (vs. $0.46-0.48 guidance). TENB has beaten both revenue and EPS consensus in each of the past 20 quarters. The stock is up 50.2% since late April, sharply outperforming S&P 500 (+3.9%); options imply ~16.5% move. Short interest at 10%.

bullets.title: FTNT: Q2 earnings preview flagged; FTNT in focus this week
bullets.body: StreetAccount published a Q2 consensus metrics preview for Fortinet ahead of its earnings report. No directional view provided in the sourced item; monitoring for results.

bullets.title: RBLX: Week 30 CCUs flat at 16.4M; 2Q bookings tracking low-end, Citi maintains Buy
bullets.body: Roblox week 30 average peak CCUs were 16.4M, flat sequentially but down 15% YoY. 2Q26 data tracks to ~$1.57B bookings, slightly below mid-point guidance of $1.55-1.61B. Early 3Q26 data is consistent with Citi's $1.87B forecast. Citi maintains Buy.

bullets.title: UBER: At 52-week low; Pelosi calls underwater; pre-market slight recovery
bullets.body: UBER hit a 52-week low this morning, trading below Nancy Pelosi's May call entry per social media commentary. StreetAccount confirmed UBER at $66.50, -26.8% on a 52-week basis. The stock is also mentioned as one of 12 names hitting 52-week lows in today's screen.

bullets.title: WBD: Seaport downgrade drives 185% options volume spike; Paramount merger delayed to June 2027
bullets.body: WBD was downgraded by Seaport Research Partners, triggering 185% above-average options volume (195,673 vs. 105,811 avg). Separately, Paramount (PSKY) and WBD agreed to delay their $110B merger until June 2027 due to state AG legal challenges, despite EU clearance; a Wolfe Research expert call on the DOJ risk is scheduled for July 29.

bullets.title: HOOD: JPM models strong 2Q — prediction market volumes, transaction revenue +21% QoQ
bullets.body: JPM models Robinhood 2Q transaction revenue at $757M (+21% QoQ, +40% YoY) with prediction market volumes of 13B contracts. Net interest revenue modeled at $427M on a ~$20B margin book. HOOD announced a 10% headcount reduction with ~$20M cash charge. KeyBanc maintains $125 PT (66x FY26 EPS). HOOD was at a 52-week low per today's screen.

bullets.title: CVNA: 22V recommends put spreads ahead of 7/29 earnings; technicals mirror TSLA pre-drop setup
bullets.body: 22V Research recommends buying CVNA July 31st $56/$46 put spreads (~$1.80 debit, 4.5x max payoff) ahead of Tuesday earnings, noting CVNA's technicals mirror TSLA's setup prior to its 17% two-day post-earnings decline. Options are pricing 11.7% implied move vs. a 17%+ historical average on 9 of last 10 reports.

bullets.title: FICO/EFX/TRU: JPM hosting VantageScore CEO call Thursday on Fannie/Freddie mortgage delivery
bullets.body: JPMorgan is hosting an investor call Thursday at 12pm ET with VantageScore CEO Silvio Tavares to discuss competitive positioning vs. FICO following Fannie/Freddie beginning to take delivery of VantageScore-backed mortgage loans in April 2026. VantageScore is jointly owned by Equifax, Experian, and TransUnion.
